mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last two months signals an improving labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals strong economic demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the GDP is increasing, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production index by more than 1% over the last month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points over the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% over the last two months signals easing inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real income and purchasing power increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between CPI decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the real GDP growth rate is negative, it signals a restrictive monetary policy coupled with a demand contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and negative GDP growth on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over two consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and related economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts are increasing, or if the correlation between housing starts and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
